declarations.statement: (hτ : ‹TopologicalSpace N› ≤ τc) (harc : ∀ a z : N, C.le ⊤ a z → ∃ c : ℝ → N, C.CausalCurveOn ⊤ c 0 1 ∧ c 0 = a ∧ c 1 = z) (hp : ∀ c, C.CausalCurveOn ⊤ c 0 1 → CM.CausalCurveOn ⊤ (p ∘ c) 0 1) (hD : ∀ c, C.CausalCurveOn ⊤ c 0 1 → CX.CausalCurveOn ⊤ (D ∘ c) 0 1) (hM : CM.StronglyCausal) (hX : CX.StronglyCausal) (hB : (∀ x : N, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun WV : Set M × Set X => IsOpen WV.1 ∧ p x ∈ WV.1 ∧ IsOpen WV.2 ∧ D x ∈ WV.2) (fun WV => @connectedComponentIn N τc (p ⁻¹' WV.1) x ∩ D ⁻¹' WV.2))) : C.StronglyCausal
declarations.standing: {M : Type v} {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace M] [TopologicalSpace X] {CM : Causality M} {CX : Causality X} {N : Type u} (τc : TopologicalSpace N) [TopologicalSpace N] {C : Causality N} {p : N → M} {D : N → X}: the binders of the original, in its order. τc is bound before the instance, so the instance is N's topology everywhere except inside @connectedComponentIn N τc. readings.reading: ∀ a z, C.le ⊤ a z → ∃ c, C.CausalCurveOn ⊤ c 0 1 ∧ c 0 = a ∧ c 1 = z: ≤ at N (⊤) realised by causal curves of ⊤ over [0, 1], exactly the binder of mem_connectedComponentIn_diamond_of_curves and le_top_map_of_curves.
readings.why: the dispatch's and the target's form, and what the proof uses

readings.reading: Hereditary gluing, ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W, for N, M and X. It implies the M-only form (GluingModels.absolutelyMinimal_of_forall), so the refutation also covers the M-only reading of OQ-95, and DEC-167's per-open-set gluing axiom (kb/0285).
readings.why: the strongest gluing hypothesis, placed inside the negated ∀, gives the strongest refutation

Causal.not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves refutes the printed form; a positive stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves would read as the statement it negates. The glued refutation keeps _of_curves in that sense (not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves_glued).

findings: F1, gluing and continuity do not rescue the printed form. Causal.not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves_glued (scaffold/CausalScaffold/StrongCausalityLiftsCurves.lean:330) is one statement. Inside the negated ∀ it has ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for N, M and X, Continuous p and Continuous D, and the rest of not_stronglyCausal_lift_of_curves (Causal/StrongCausalityLifts.lean:649), the curve hypothesis in its strongest reading. The witness is symmRationalLine into the timelike line with p = D = id (symmRationalLine_separates_lift_glued, :305). It fails exactly harc (symmRationalLine_not_le_realised, :287), and also causality (:274), tarentin (:280) and causal arc-connectedness. So the refutation says nothing about a causal or tarentin M̃. The parent's antisymmetric variant (REPORT F1 of T-abs-strong-causality-lifts) is still argued only, not in Lean.

F2 (positive), the amendment in harc form. With ≤ of N at ⊤ realised by causal curves over [0, 1] in place of causal arc-connectedness, the target holds: stronglyCausal_lift_of_le_realised (:84), alexandrovTopology_eq_lift_of_le_realised (:100), stronglyCausalOpen_lift_of_le_realised (:115), stronglyCausal_lift_of_weakMorphism_of_le_realised (:130) and stronglyCausal_lift_self_of_le_realised (:146). The CausallyArcConnected originals (Causal/StrongCausalityLifts.lean:334, :349, :362, :377, :392) are corollaries (examples at :167–190).

F3: the harc forms are strictly more general, at least without gluing. orderLine (Causal/Morphism.lean:804, the order of ℝ restricted to each open set) is not causally arc-connected (0 ≤ 2 in ℝ ∖ {1}, :233), yet ≤ at ⊤ is realised by segments (:221). Its causal curves at ⊤ are the timelike line's (:207), and the harc forms give StronglyCausal and StronglyCausalOpen (:252). It is not absolutely minimal (GluingModels.orderLine_not_minimal). Under gluing, whether harc is strictly weaker than CausallyArcConnected is not settled in Lean. Argued only, not in Lean, as a follow-up candidate: on ℝ, the timelike ≤ with x ≪_U y iff x < y, [x, y] ⊆ U and x ≠ 0. It should be a causality (I⁻ is the timelike one minus {0}) and hereditarily absolutely minimal (subdivide avoiding 0). It has harc, and ≪_ℝ(−1, 1) has no chronal curve (one would pass 0 at an interior time, and its ≪-step from there fails).
questions: Q1 (OQ-145, for the author, not decided here): which hypothesis does the statement of record take, ≤ of M̃ realised by causal curves (harc, the weaker), or M̃ causally arc-connected? Both forms are now in Lean, and the harc form implies the other. Reading taken: none chosen. The file states both, and its docstring calls the harc forms 'the amendment of OQ-145, not the printed form'.

Q2 (reading of 'realised by causal curves'): harc asks for a curve over [0, 1] at ⊤. Reading taken: [0, 1] stands for any compact parameter segment (affine reparametrisation, not proved here), at ⊤ only, not in every open U. CausallyArcConnected asks it in every U and for ≪ as well. If the author means the per-open-set form, that is CausallyArcConnected's ≤ half, between the two.

Q3, for the instantiating closers (T-loc-btz-tamifying-initial, T-loc-ealpha-tamifying-alexandrov): the forms to cite are now Causal.Causality.*_of_le_realised. They need harc only for btzCylCausality (or the cover) and for Ẽ_α, not CausallyArcConnected. This is the parent's Q4 carried over, not a new reading.
